job_application.reformulated_text:
A job applicant submits job applications to various companies. Each company confirms receipt of the job application and rates it. The applicant can then negotiate a job interview with the company. If the company wants the applicant to work for them, the applicant enters the probation phase. 

During the probation phase, the applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the applicant. After the probation phase, if the job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless the applicant rated the company C or less. In this case, the applicant continues to receive job offers but no longer has to report job applications.

maternity_leave.reformulated_text:
To support planning, taking, and extending a maternity leave, the following process can be created:

1. Fetch information about potential maternity leave models, including their duration in months and the options for splitting the leave between parents.
2. Present the parent with a selection of these models to choose from.
3. Collect relevant information from the parent, such as their leave preferences and requirements.
4. Notify the Social Security and Company of the parent's intention to take maternity leave, ensuring timely notification.
5. Gather information from the Company regarding their maternity leave policies and any necessary procedures.
6. At the end of the maternity leave period, allow the parent to decide whether to extend their leave.

evidence.entity_name: 6. At the end of the maternity leave period, allow the parent to decide whether to extend their leave.

job_application.reformulated_text: The process involves two entities: the job applicant and the company. A job application is created when a job applicant submits an application to a company. The company must confirm receipt of the application and rate it. A job interview can be negotiated. When a company wants the job applicant to work for them, the job applicant enters the probation phase. After the probation phase, the job applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the job applicant. Reviews for a company can only be seen by job applicants after 1 year, the text does not specify whether this is a separate condition or a change in visibility of existing reviews. If a job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless the job applicant rated the company C or less, in which case the process continues, but the job applicant no longer has to report job applications. The text does not specify what happens to the job application while the job applicant is in the probation phase, nor whether the job applicant can rate the company before the probation phase ends.

maternity_leave.reformulated_text: The process involves two entities: the leave and the parent. The leave is created when the parent decides to take a maternity leave. The process starts with fetching information about potential leave models, which include the duration in months and the split between parents. The parent then selects a leave model. The process collects relevant information from the parent. The parent is notified to inform Social Security and the company in time. The process also gathers information from the company. At the end of the leave period, the parent decides whether to extend the leave. The text does not specify what happens if the parent decides to extend the leave, nor what the process does with the leave while the parent is deciding.

work_accident.reformulated_text:
The process involves several entities: the accident, the insured employment, the employer, the employee, the Labour Inspectorate, the accident insurance provider, and the competent directorate. 

A work accident is considered to be an accident that occurs in the following circumstances: 
- the accident occurs in a location, at a time and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment
- when working from home
- on the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work, to lunch or on the way home, whereby carpools are also protected
- for training sessions that serve to provide specific professional knowledge, whereby an accident on the way to or from the training centre is considered a work accident
- on the direct route from home, or from the workplace or training centre to a doctor and back, if this interrupts the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work or the route home (the doctor's visit must be notified to the employer in advance)
- on the way to or from the workplace or training centre with the purpose of taking a child to or collecting them from a childcare facility, a daycare facility, external care or a school, insofar as they have a supervisory responsibility for the child
- when making use of advocacy groups or professional associations (e.g. Chamber of Labour, trade union federation, guild etc.)

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren and students, an accident is considered to be a work accident if, amongst other things:
- the accident occurs in a location, at a time and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education or the compulsory kindergarten year that forms the basis of the insurance
- when taking part in a school event or school-related event
- on the direct route from the child's place of residence or permanent accommodation to kindergarten or a school visit or on the way home
- when performing a practical task prescribed as part of the curriculum and/or the study regulations
- in certain professional (training) orientations

In an agricultural or forestry establishment, accidents can be considered work accidents if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment, including working in the household of the owner, providing accommodation for guests, secondary occupations for selling agricultural products, building work for the establishment, and neighbourhood assistance for another establishment.

Certain accidents are considered the same as work accidents outside of professional activity, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services, assisting with an accident or donating blood, and training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation (fire brigade, water rescue, Red Cross, Alpine Rescue, air rescue, etc.).

The employee must inform the employer immediately of: any work accident, any incident that would almost have led to an accident, any serious and immediate risk to safety and health that they discover, any defect discovered in protection systems. The employer must immediately report any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate, if it has not been reported to the emergency services.

The accident insurance provider must be notified of every work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed, or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days, in full or in part, within five days. As a self-employed person, accidents involving people you employ and those that involve you must be reported to the accident insurance provider in good time.

Students and schoolchildren should report accidents to the competent directorate. Schools, educational facilities and universities are obliged to report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible accident insurance provider in triplicate.

In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported.
